text: Welcome to week 10 of the official
Arkhamard's iRacing series. And this
week, you'll be doing battle at the
Daytona International Speedway for 20
laps. For qualifying this week, you'll
want to prioritize keeping your tires as
cool as possible. With cooler tires,
you'll deal with less rolling
resistance, and with less rolling
resistance, you'll reach higher top
speeds down the straightaways. Shift
into fourth gear and slowly pull out of
the pit lane, easing onto the throttle
as you reach 101 mph. By running 101 and
nothing less, you'll avoid triggering
iRacing's qualifying scrutiny, and
you'll be able to keep your tire
temperatures down until you ease further
onto the gas in turns three and four of
your warm-up lap. Your left side tires
between the outside seam and the dotted
white lines as you build speed through
your first lap. Keep the wheels steady
and keep the car away from the wall as
running too high would dump air on your
spoiler and cost you momentum as you
come around to take your hot lap.
As you run the car against the yellow
line in the trioval, you want to allow
the car to track out to the center on
exit. In doing so, not only will you
avoid scrubbing off speed by giving it
more wheel, but you'll also be able to
make use of the banking. This will be
the case through every corner. Slowly
point the car down the track as you
enter turn one. Run through the corner,
keeping your wheel as steady as you can.
As you exit, keep your wheel angle
consistent and slowly open it back up as
the car tracks up. Enjoy the extra speed
down the backstretch as you slowly point
the car back down towards the banking in

Once the race rolls around, the initial
advantage will go to whichever lane
coordinates a better start. In this
case, the outside did a better job
lining up. And as a result, they were
able to surge ahead at the beginning. As
the inside builds strength, it'll become
the ideal lane. But with the right cars
in the middle and outside lanes, they
can compensate for the additional
distance. One of the biggest ongoing
issues with this car is its sensitivity
to contact. You'll notice that I give
the 34 a small tap when he comes down.
This gave me a 4x and staggered the
inside line as a result. It also
frustrated me, so I decided against
helping him and rolled out of the
throttle. This bogged down the inside
line and allowed the top to roll several
car lengths ahead of us. That just goes
to show how vital cooperation is with
this draft model. Speaking of the draft
model, if the race becomes single file
around the inside, which I have seen
happen more often than not, it will
become difficult to get a run going
unless you have people to help you. If
you get a run on the car ahead of you
and pull out of line, you will only have
a couple seconds to capitalize on your
run before you get hit by a wall of air.
In such a situation, the side draft can
only get you so far. If you want to make
guaranteed progress, you'll need help,
and competent help at that. The worst
thing you can do for your line is insist
on leading it when you can't hold your
wheel steady. Through the corners and
straightaways, you'll want to
demonstrate the same finesse as what got
you to the front in qualifying. Dig your
elbow into your ribs if you have to, as
weaving back and forth will give your
pusher a hard time centering their
bumper to yours and may wreck you as a
result. If you can hold a pretty wheel,
understand the consequences of the moves
you make, and throw in a little bit of
luck, you'll find yourself fighting for
the win as the race winds down. Good
luck.
